units.title: 3.1 Section A: The study of religions: beliefs and teachings

outcomes.text: Study the beliefs and teachings of two of Christianity, Islam, Judaism and Buddhism and their influence on people.
Explain Christian beliefs through scripture and authority, noting Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant views.
Explain God as omnipotent, loving and just, and the problem of evil and suffering.
Explain the oneness of God and the Trinity of Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
Compare Christian beliefs about creation, including the Word and Spirit in John 1 and Genesis 1.
Compare Christian beliefs about resurrection, judgement, heaven and hell.
Explain the incarnation, Jesus as Son of God, and the crucifixion, resurrection and ascension.
Explain sin and original sin, and salvation through law, grace and Spirit.
Explain the role of Christ in salvation and the idea of atonement.
Explain Islamic beliefs through the Qur'an and other authority, noting Sunni and Shi'a views.
Compare the six articles of faith in Sunni Islam with the five roots of Usul ad-Din in Shi'a Islam.

subtopics.title: Tawhid and the nature of God

outcomes.text: Explain Tawhid (Surah 112) and God's omnipotence, mercy, justice, immanence and transcendence.
Describe angels, including Jibril and Mika'il.
Explain predestination, human freedom and the Day of Judgement.
Explain Akhirah: accountability, resurrection, heaven and hell.
Explain Risalah and the role of Adam, Ibrahim and Muhammad.
Explain the authority of the Qur'an and the earlier holy books.
Explain the role and significance of the imamate in Shi'a Islam.
Explain Jewish beliefs through scripture and authority, noting Orthodox, Reform and Liberal views.
Explain God as one, Creator, Law-Giver and Judge, loving and merciful, and the Shekhinah.
Explain Jewish beliefs about life after death, judgement and resurrection.
Explain the nature and role of the Messiah and differing views.
Explain the promised land and Covenant with Abraham, and the Sinai Covenant with Moses and the Ten Commandments.
Explain moral principles: justice, healing the world, charity, kindness and Pikuach Nefesh.
Explain free will and the 613 mitzvot, and mitzvot between man and God and between people.
Explain Buddhist beliefs through sacred texts, noting Theravada, Mahayana, Zen and Pure Land views.
Explain the Dhamma and dependent arising.
Explain anicca, anatta and dukkha.
Compare the Five Aggregates in Theravada with sunyata and Buddha-nature in Mahayana.
Compare the Arhat and Bodhisattva ideals, Buddhahood and the Pure Land.
Describe the Buddha's birth, life of luxury, the Four Sights, ascetic life and Enlightenment.
Explain suffering, its causes (the Three Poisons), the end of craving and nibbana.
Explain the Eightfold Path as the Threefold Way of ethics, meditation and wisdom.
Explain kamma, rebirth, compassion and loving kindness.
List the five moral precepts and the six perfections of Mahayana Buddhism.

units.title: 3.2 Section B: Thematic studies: religious, philosophical and ethical studies

subtopics.title: Studying religion and belief in society

outcomes.text: Study religious and non-religious beliefs, including atheism and humanism, on the issues raised.
Explain contrasting beliefs on contraception, sex before marriage and same-sex relationships.
Explain human sexuality and religious views on sex before and outside marriage.
Explain contraception, family planning, and the nature and purpose of marriage.
Explain views on same-sex marriage and cohabitation.
Explain reasons for divorce, remarriage and arguments from the sanctity of vows and compassion.
Explain the roles of parents and children, and extended and nuclear families.
Explain the purposes of families: procreation, stability, protecting children and faith education.
Explain contemporary family issues such as same-sex parents and polygamy.
Explain the roles of men and women and gender equality.
Give examples of gender prejudice and discrimination.

topics.title: 3.2.2 Theme B: Religion, peace and conflict

subtopics.title: Contrasting views on peace and conflict

outcomes.text: Explain contrasting beliefs on violence, weapons of mass destruction and pacifism.
Explain the meaning of peace, justice, forgiveness and reconciliation.
Explain religious views on violence and violent protest, and terrorism.
Explain reasons for war: greed, self-defence and retaliation.
Explain the just war theory and its criteria, and holy war.
Explain pacifism.
Explain religion and belief as a cause of war and violence now.
Explain nuclear weapons, deterrence and views on using weapons of mass destruction.
Explain religious peace-making and the work of individuals inspired by religious teaching.
Describe how a present-day religious organisation responds to victims of war.
